title: Overlap of two availability lists
prompt:
Given two sorted lists of disjoint inclusive ranges, return every range of points covered by both lists, sorted by start.

- Each list has 0 to 50,000 [start, end] pairs sorted by start, with integers 0 <= start <= end <= 10^9.
- Within one list no two ranges share a point.
- Sharing a single point counts: [1, 3] and [3, 5] intersect in [3, 3].
- Return one [start, end] pair per overlapping pair of ranges, sorted by start.
hints: Comparing every range in one list with every range in the other is O(n·m). Both lists are sorted, so walk them together.
Keep one pointer per list. The overlap of the two current ranges is [max(starts), min(ends)] when that is non-empty.
Then advance the pointer whose range ends first; it cannot overlap anything further in the other list.

solution.explanation: Two closed ranges overlap exactly on [max of starts, min of ends] when that is non-empty. The range that ends first cannot reach the next range in the other list, because that list is sorted and disjoint, so it is safe to drop. Each step discards one range, so the merge-like walk is linear and produces results already in order.

complexity.notes: Extra space excludes the output list, which can hold up to n + m - 1 ranges.

followUps: Intersect k sorted lists at once. How does a heap or pairwise folding compare?
